spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: Compact support localizes Weil's global positivity criterion: each test function sees only finitely many prime powers, turning RH into a nested family of finite-prime quadratic-form questions without making those questions automatically tractable.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The explicit formula defines local distributions W_v and a Weil quadratic form. RH is stated as equivalent to a sign condition on W_v(g*g*) for all compactly supported g satisfying transform constraints. If g has bounded multiplicative support, W_p vanishes for all sufficiently large p, so each instance uses finitely many primes.
directed.conceptual_reading: Locality in support removes the infinite Euler product from each individual check while preserving the global universal quantifier over scales and test functions.
directed.representation_or_bridge: Mellin/Fourier transform and involutive convolution bridge zeros to a quadratic form assembled from archimedean and prime-local terms.
directed.boundary_or_failure: Numerically established archimedean positivity has no supplied mechanism guaranteed to persist after prime terms are added; finite locality alone does not prove the universal criterion.
directed.uncertainty: The localization principle is explicit, but sign conventions and transform constraints are formula-sensitive.

supported: The Weil-form equivalence, compact-support localization to finitely many primes, universal quantification over test functions/scales, and the lack of a mechanism extending archimedean positivity are explicit.
inference: Calling this a nested family of finite-prime questions is a reasonable interpretation of the universal criterion.
paraphrase_or_style_risk: The output gives a real localization operation, but 'a sign condition' is too generic for a criterion whose direction is mathematically essential.
context_or_ocr_risk: Sign conventions and the exact Fourier/Mellin transform constraints are formula-sensitive, so they must be copied cautiously rather than omitted.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: Exponentiating rho log x aliases infinitely many values of rho, so Li(x^rho) forgets exactly the information needed to define the zero sum; Ei(rho log x) restores a single-valued variable before conditional summation.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The letter notes that x^rho is unchanged when rho is shifted by 2pi i n/log x, making a literal sum of Li(x^rho) repeat essentially the same values. Von Mangoldt's replacement Ei(rho log x) retains rho and gives the meaningful term in Riemann's conditionally interpreted prime-counting formula.
directed.conceptual_reading: A many-to-one coordinate change is harmless for isolated evaluation but fatal inside an indexed infinite sum because it erases the index's branch data.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The logarithmic lift rho log x bridges the traditional integral-logarithm notation to a well-defined single-valued summand; test functions then connect it to Guinand-Weil formulas.
directed.boundary_or_failure: Branch cuts and ordering of the conditional zero sum remain essential even after repairing the variable.
directed.uncertainty: The aliasing counterexample and repair are explicit; exact branch conventions require scan verification.

supported: The invariance of x^rho under rho shifts, the resulting repetition problem, the Ei(rho log x) repair, and the Guinand-Weil test-function connection are explicit.
inference: Describing exponentiation as a many-to-one coordinate change that erases index data is a faithful reading of the counterexample.
unsupported_or_imported: The boundary claim about ordering a conditionally convergent zero sum is not stated in this exact letter slice; it is imported from the earlier survey unit.
